title: Scenario Dreamer: Vectorized Latent Diffusion for Generating Driving Simulation Environments

control_signal.value: Behaviour: tilting strength kappa on the return model (collision-with-ego reward) for good or adversarial agents. Scene: number of lanes and agents; known map or partial scene for inpainting; simulation-compatibility flag.

control_mechanism.value: Exponential tilting of a learned return distribution in a return-conditioned multi-agent Transformer (CtRL-Sim); scene density set by specifying (No, Nl) before latent sampling; map or inpainting conditioning; classifier guidance for simulation-compatible scenes.

base_model.value: Transformer VAE on vectorized lanes and agent boxes, plus latent diffusion with factorized attention and AdaLN-Zero conditioning; CtRL-Sim return-conditioned autoregressive Transformer for behaviour.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset and nuPlan for generation; RL planners trained in GPUDrive on 100 Waymo scenes and evaluated on 250 scenes.

metrics.value: Lane graph: FD, connectivity/density, reachability, route length, generation time. Agents: JSD metrics and collision rate. Behaviour: JSD, agent and planner collision rate. RL: collision, offroad, success rates.

controllability_evidence.value: Planner collision rate 4.9% with kappa=+10 versus 11.9% with kappa=-50, with only modest JSD change. RL planner success falls from 38.2% to 32.1% under negative tilting on 100m scenes.

stated_limitations.value: Traffic light signaling of lanes did not always give valid traffic logic; only centerline maps are generated, other road elements are future work.

notes: Mixed control: adversarial behaviour via return tilting (main steering), scene density via conditioning counts. Family chosen from the adversarial-behaviour mechanism.
